questions.stem:
A research project into food purchases found that 35% of people who buy eggs do not buy free range eggs.

A random sample of 30 people who bought eggs is taken. The random variable $F$ denotes the number of people who do not buy free range eggs.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Writing or using $1-\mathrm{P}(F \leqslant 11)$
A1: awrt 0.345
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $\mathrm{P}(F\geqslant 12)=1-\mathrm{P}(F\leqslant 11) = 0.34517\ldots$ awrt 0.345

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: $\mathrm{P}(F \leqslant 14)-\mathrm{P}(F \leqslant 7)$
A1: awrt 0.811
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $\mathrm{P}(8\leqslant F<15)=\mathrm{P}(F\leqslant 14)-\mathrm{P}(F\leqslant 7) =0.81104\ldots$ awrt 0.811

parts.label: c
parts.text:
A farm shop gives 3 loyalty points with every purchase of free range eggs. With every purchase of eggs that are not free range the farm shop gives 1 loyalty point.
A random sample of 30 customers who buy eggs from the farm shop is taken.

(c) Find the probability that the total number of points given to these customers is less than 70
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: $3(30-F)+F<70$ or $F>10$, or $3(30-R)+3R<70$ or $R<20$ (allow equation instead of inequality, may be implied by 2nd M1)
M1: Writing or using $1-\mathrm{P}(F \leqslant 10)$ ft their 10 but must be finding the correct tail
A1: awrt 0.492
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $3(R)+30-R<70$ or $R<20$ M1
- $\mathrm{P}(R<20)=\mathrm{P}(R\leqslant 19)$ M1
- $\mathrm{P}(F>10)=1-\mathrm{P}(F\leqslant 10) = 0.4922\ldots$ awrt 0.492

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The manager of the farm shop believes that the proportion of customers who buy eggs but do not buy free range eggs is more than 35%

In a survey of 200 customers who buy eggs, 86 do not buy free range eggs.

Using a suitable test and a normal approximation,

(d) determine, at the 5% level of significance, whether there is evidence to support the manager's belief. State your hypotheses clearly.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) B1: $\mathrm{H_0}: p=0.35$, $\mathrm{H_1}: p>0.35$ (both hypotheses in terms of $p$ or $\pi$)
M1: Writing or using a normal distribution with a mean of 70 (Let $Y$ be the number of customers who do not buy free range eggs. $Y \sim \mathrm{N}(70, 45.5)$)
M1: Standardising using 85.5/86/86.5, their mean and their sd, e.g. $\mathrm{P}(Y\geqslant 86)\approx \mathrm{P}\left(Z>\frac{85.5-70}{\sqrt{45.5}}\right)$ or $\pm\frac{x-0.5-70}{\sqrt{45.5}}=1.6449$
M1: Using a continuity correction $86\pm0.5$
A1: $\approx 0.01078...$ or $81.595...$ (correct probability awrt 0.0108 or awrt 0.0107 or $x$ value of awrt 82; or allow awrt 2.29 and 1.6449 seen; NB exact Binomial 0.01156, Po approx awrt 0.0352)
dM1: (dep on 1st M1) A correct statement based on comparing 86 with their CR or their prob with 0.05 [condone 0.989>0.95] - contradicting non-contextual comments M0. There is evidence to reject $\mathrm{H_0}$. In the critical region
A1: There is evidence to support the manager's belief / There is evidence to support the proportion of customers who do not buy free range eggs is more than 35% (o.e.) (a correct statement in context; NB award M1A1 for a correct contextual statement on its own)
